text: APIs, or Application Programming Interfaces, allow different software systems to communicate with each other. When working with APIs, you typically send HTTP requests to a server, which then responds with data, often in JSON format. JSON is a lightweight text format that is easy for both humans and machines to read. Most APIs require authentication, usually through an API key, to ensure that only authorized users have access. Additionally, you must be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a given time period. Finally, good error handling is essential; when an API fails, you need to understand error codes to fix your request or adapt your code.
